Reduced respiratory and bulbar muscle force can contribute to a weak neonatal cry; the clinical cohort documents the finding without testing the intervening physiology.
Respiratory muscle involvement can contribute to neonatal distress. Palatal, pulmonary and aspiration-related factors can also contribute, so this is an inferred, nonexclusive route.
Facial muscle weakness contributes to the characteristic myopathic facial appearance.
Proximal weakness is part of the clinical distribution of the generalized muscle disorder.
Weak suck and bulbar dysfunction contribute to feeding difficulty alongside palatal and mandibular abnormalities; the route is multifactorial.
Bulbar muscle dysfunction can contribute to impaired swallowing; cohort data establish dysphagia, while its individual contribution relative to structural abnormalities remains uncertain.
Reduced force and mobility can delay motor acquisition. Contractures and other complications also affect function; the clinical literature does not isolate their relative contributions.
Respiratory muscle weakness can contribute to a restrictive ventilatory defect, with spinal or chest-wall abnormalities and aspiration-related lung disease modifying severity.

nodes.description: Patients with biallelic pathogenic STAC3 variants are susceptible to malignant hyperthermia after volatile anesthetics or succinylcholine. nodes.description: Biallelic STAC3 variants impair the skeletal-muscle adaptor. The recurrent hypomorphic missense allele c.851G>C (p.Trp284Ser) affects the first SH3 domain; splice-altering, frameshift and truncating alleles also occur. Loss of the SH3 interaction with the CaV1.1 II-III loop severely reduces calcium release while allowing residual channel-complex association through the N-terminal region. Complete loss in experimental models can additionally reduce junctional channel abundance.

evidence.snippet: Congenital myopathy-13 (CMYP13), also known as Bailey-Bloch congenital myopathy and Native American myopathy (NAM), is a condition caused by biallelic missense pathogenic variants in STAC3, which encodes an important protein necessary for the excitation-relaxation coupling machinery in the muscle.

evidence.reference_title: STAC3 disorder: a common cause of congenital hypotonia in Southern African patients.
evidence.snippet: The spread of this variant worldwide and the allele frequency higher in the African/African-American ancestry than the Admixed Americans, strongly indicates that the STAC3 c.851 G > C variant has an African origin which may be due to an ancient mutation with migration and population bottlenecks.

evidence.reference_title: STAC3 related congenital myopathy: A case series of seven Comorian patients.
evidence.snippet: Local history and geography may explain the overrepresentation of NAM in the Comorian Archipelago with a founder effect.

nodes.description: Increased skeletal-muscle lipids have been reported in patients, but their causal role in weakness is unresolved. A CRISPR stac3-null zebrafish study reported elevated neutral lipids from 5 days post-fertilization alongside cytoskeletal and myogenic abnormalities. The available abstract does not establish that its bulk lipid measurements are muscle-specific or prove lipid accumulation mediates the coupling defect.

animal_models.description: Reproduces elevated neutral lipids alongside muscle abnormalities in larvae; muscle-specific lipid localization is not established by the available abstract.

evidence.reference_title: Early life lipid overload in Native American Myopathy is phenocopied by stac3 knockout in zebrafish.
evidence.snippet: These muscle alterations were associated with elevated neutral lipid levels starting at 5 dpf and persisting beyond 7 dpf.

evidence.reference_title: Early life lipid overload in Native American Myopathy is phenocopied by stac3 knockout in zebrafish.
evidence.snippet: Clinically, NAM patients demonstrated increased lipids in skeletal muscle, but it is unclear if neutral lipids are associated with altered muscle function in NAM.

nodes.description: Direct RyR activation by 4-chloro-m-cresol restored calcium release and contractility in cultured Stac3-null myotubes. This pharmacological bypass is a mechanistic experiment, not evidence for clinical agonist treatment.
Congenital clubfoot, reported in 59% of the Southern African clinical cohort and in Brazilian cases.

evidence.reference_title: STAC3 disorder: a common cause of congenital hypotonia in Southern African patients.
evidence.snippet: Of the clinical group, 93% had a palatal abnormality, 52% a spinal anomaly, 59% had talipes equinovarus deformity/deformities, 38% had arthrogryposis multiplex congenita, and 22% had a history suggestive of malignant hyperthermia.

nodes.description: Male mice underwent inducible deletion of Stac3 exons 2-5 at four weeks and were assessed four weeks later. Limb muscle retained roughly 30% or less STAC3 protein despite near-absent transcript. Body and muscle growth, fiber cross-sectional area and grip strength declined; central nuclei increased without a change in total fiber number. The CAG driver is not muscle-specific.
A weak cry at birth was recorded in 16/17 (94%) patients with data.

evidence.reference_title: STAC3 disorder: a common cause of congenital hypotonia in Southern African patients.
evidence.snippet: A weak cry at birth (16/17 (94%)) and neonatal hypotonia (27/28 (96%)) were almost universally present in the patients.

nodes.description: A CRISPR knockout used to follow early skeletal muscle development, which surfaced neutral lipid accumulation alongside the expected weakness.

The forward-genetic stac3 mi34 splice-donor mutant has severely reduced muscle calcium transients and locomotion. Early triads and contractile responses to caffeine were preserved, but myofibers broke down during larval development. Maternal stac3 transcript can contribute residual early function; a translation-blocking morpholino intensified immotility.

Electron microscopy, electrophysiology and dynamic imaging showed reduced DHPR levels, functionality and stability in stac3-mutant muscle. NAM preparations also showed increased caffeine-evoked release and internal-store calcium without altered caffeine sensitivity. The retrieved abstract does not establish a genomic knock-in design.

evidence.reference_title: Congenital myopathy results from misregulation of a muscle Ca2+ channel by mutant Stac3.
evidence.snippet: stac3NAM myofibers exhibited increased caffeine-induced Ca2+ release across a wide range of concentrations in the absence of altered caffeine sensitivity as well as increased Ca2+ in internal stores
